capabilities.name: Video Ingestion & Recording
capabilities.notes: The repository explicitly provisions a 'vss-video-analytics-api' service via Docker Compose for standalone video ingestion. It supports both live streams and recorded archives, as indicated by the README's mention of 'Search video streams or archives' and the API setup skill.

capabilities.name: Object Detection & Classification
capabilities.notes: The README explicitly lists 'object detection, tracking' as part of the perception pipeline for alert verification. The architecture relies on NVIDIA NIM microservices (likely Cosmos or similar) for this, which are external dependencies not fully contained in this repo's source code but are integral to the blueprint's function.

capabilities.name: Object Tracking
capabilities.notes: Explicitly mentioned alongside object detection in the 'Alert Verification' workflow description. The system processes trajectories and incidents, implying tracking capabilities within the perception stack.

capabilities.name: GPU Hardware Utilization
capabilities.notes: The blueprint is described as 'GPU-accelerated'. The README lists hardware requirements. While the specific analytics API skill allows CPU-only testing for validation, the core architecture and NIM microservices (Cosmos, Nemotron) are designed for GPU execution.

capabilities.name: Natural Language Video Search
capabilities.notes: A primary feature of the VSS blueprint is searching video archives using natural language queries via RAG and embeddings.

capabilities.name: Video Summarization
capabilities.notes: The blueprint supports long-video summarization through chunking and aggregation of dense captions using LLMs.

capabilities.name: Visual Q&A
capabilities.notes: Users can ask visual questions about video content, with answers generated by VLMs.

constraints: Requires NVIDIA GPU for VLM/LLM inference (Cosmos/Nemotron)
Internet access for pulling NIM images or model weights

assumptions: The user has access to NVIDIA NIM microservices or equivalent VLM/LLM endpoints.
MQTT broker is available externally for detection metadata publication (not implemented in this repo).
GPU hardware is provisioned and drivers are installed.

evidence.claim: The repository provisions a 'vss-video-analytics-api' service for video ingestion via Docker Compose.
The blueprint performs object detection, tracking, and alert verification using perception and VLMs.
The system is GPU-accelerated and uses NVIDIA NIM microservices.
A CLI tool 'vss_cli' is available for interacting with the VSS services.

validation.judge_notes: REVISE: [critical] The rubric requires 'verified' status to be supported by code/test evidence. The provided evidence for this claim is a Python script that *generates* deployment tasks (`.github/skill-eval/adapters/.../generate.py`) and README text. It does not contain the actual ingestion logic, API implementation, or Docker Compose service definition itself. Furthermore, the generate.py excerpt explicitly states the standalone analytics API is 'CPU-only' (`gpu_count: 0`), which contradicts the passport's claim that this specific capability relies on GPU hardware for its core function. | [high] The passport claims this capability is verified, but the only code-level evidence cited (`generate.py`) describes a test environment that explicitly *skips* GPU enforcement (`gpu_count: 0`). The README mentions hardware requirements, which counts as 'declared' marketing text, not 'verified' code evidence. There is no source code in the excerpts showing GPU tensor operations or CUDA initialization. | [high] The claim is supported only by README text ('primary feature... via RAG'). The rubric states that capabilities marked with evidence_status must be supported by an excerpt. While the README is an excerpt, it is marketing/overview text. There is no code or configuration file in the evidence showing the RAG pipeline, embedding generation, or search API implementation. | [medium] The passport lists this interface but provides no schema reference (`schema_ref: ''`) and the evidence is only README text. The rubric requires interfaces to be supported by evidence. Without a schema or code definition of the API endpoints, the specific contract (methods, parameters) is unknown. | [medium] The passport admits this is 'implied' and notes in `known_gaps` that 'No native MQTT client implementation visible... detection metadata publication to MQTT is not evidenced'. Claiming a dependency as part of the architecture without code evidence or explicit configuration in the provided excerpts is weak. The 'implied' nature suggests it might be an external integration point rather than a contained capability.

description: NVIDIA AI Blueprint for Video Search and Summarization (VSS) is a GPU-accelerated reference architecture for building video analytics agents. It ingests live or recorded video, performs object detection/classification/tracking via perception microservices, and uses Vision Language Models (VLMs) for alert verification, summarization, and natural language search. Outputs include verified alerts, summaries, and metadata.
deployment_constraints: Requires NVIDIA GPU for VLM/LLM inference (Cosmos/Nemotron)
Internet access for pulling NIM images or model weights
known_gaps: No native MQTT client implementation visible in the repository excerpts; detection metadata publication to MQTT is not evidenced in the code.
Geo-referencing of detections is not explicitly detailed in the provided excerpts, though 'spatialai-data-utils' suggests spatial capabilities.
risks: Heavy dependency on proprietary NVIDIA NIM microservices which may require specific licensing or cloud access.
Complexity of integrating multiple AI models (VLM, LLM, Perception) increases maintenance burden.
Real-time performance depends heavily on GPU availability and model latency.

adaptation_assumptions: The user has access to NVIDIA NIM microservices or equivalent VLM/LLM endpoints.
MQTT broker is available externally for detection metadata publication (not implemented in this repo).
GPU hardware is provisioned and drivers are installed.
